headline.hi: Points Ko Numbers Se Represent Karo!

subtext.hi: Coordinate Geometry mein algebra aur geometry milte hain — GPS se lekar game development tak har jagah use hota hai.
subtext.en: Coordinate Geometry is where algebra meets geometry — used everywhere from GPS to game development.

text.hi: Jab tum Google Maps par apni location dekhte ho, ya koi game character screen par move karta hai, uske peeche coordinate geometry hi kaam kar rahi hoti hai — har point ek (x, y) pair se define hota hai. Is chapter mein hum seekhenge do points ke beech ki exact distance kaise nikaalte hain — bina scale se naapo!
text.en: When you check your location on Google Maps, or a game character moves on screen, coordinate geometry is working behind it — every point is defined by an (x, y) pair. In this chapter, we'll learn how to find the exact distance between two points — without measuring with a scale!

content.hi: Coordinate plane do perpendicular lines (axes) se banta hai jahan har point ko ek unique ordered pair (x, y) se represent kiya jaata hai.
content.en: The coordinate plane is formed by two perpendicular lines (axes) where every point is represented by a unique ordered pair (x, y).

content.hi: X-axis horizontal line hai (left to right), Y-axis vertical line hai (bottom to top), aur Origin wo point hai jahan dono axes intersect karte hain (0, 0). Point (x, y) mein x ko 'abscissa' aur y ko 'ordinate' kehte hain.
content.en: The X-axis is horizontal (left to right), the Y-axis is vertical (bottom to top), and the Origin is where both axes intersect (0, 0). In a point (x, y), x is called the 'abscissa' and y the 'ordinate'.

content.hi: Coordinate plane 4 Quadrants mein baata hai: Quadrant I (x>0, y>0), Quadrant II (x<0, y>0), Quadrant III (x<0, y<0), Quadrant IV (x>0, y<0).
content.en: The coordinate plane is divided into 4 Quadrants: Quadrant I (x>0, y>0), Quadrant II (x<0, y>0), Quadrant III (x<0, y<0), Quadrant IV (x>0, y<0).

content.hi:
Yahan A(x1, y1) aur B(x2, y2) wo do points hain jinke beech distance nikal rahe ho — x1,y1 pehle point (A) ke coordinates hain, x2,y2 dusre point (B) ke.

Example: A(2, 3) aur B(5, 7) ke beech distance = √[(5-2)² + (7-3)²] = √[9+16] = √25 = 5.
content.en:
Here A(x1, y1) and B(x2, y2) are the two points whose distance you're finding — x1,y1 are the first point's (A's) coordinates, x2,y2 are the second point's (B's).

Example: distance between A(2, 3) and B(5, 7) = √[(5-2)² + (7-3)²] = √[9+16] = √25 = 5.

content.hi: Ye formula Pythagoras Theorem se derive hota hai — socho A aur B ke beech ek right-angled triangle banta hai jiske legs (x₂−x₁) aur (y₂−y₁) hain, toh hypotenuse hi unke beech ki distance hai.
content.en: This formula is derived from the Pythagoras Theorem — imagine a right-angled triangle between A and B with legs (x₂−x₁) and (y₂−y₁); the hypotenuse is exactly the distance between them.

content.hi: Ye origin se distance ka special case hai (jab ek point (0,0) hi ho). Agar point x-axis par ho (x, 0), distance = |x|; agar y-axis par ho (0, y), distance = |y|.
content.en: This is the special case of distance from the origin (when one point is (0,0)). If a point is on the x-axis (x, 0), distance = |x|; if on the y-axis (0, y), distance = |y|.

caption.hi: Do points ke beech ek right-angled triangle socho — Pythagoras Theorem hi distance formula ka base hai.
caption.en: Imagine a right-angled triangle between two points — the Pythagoras Theorem is the base of the distance formula.

question.hi: Point (x, y) mein x ko kya kehte hain?
question.en: In a point (x, y), what is x called?

explanation.hi: x-coordinate ko abscissa kehte hain, y-coordinate ko ordinate.
explanation.en: The x-coordinate is called the abscissa, the y-coordinate is the ordinate.

question.en: In which quadrant does the point (−3, 4) lie?

explanation.hi: x<0, y>0 hone par point Quadrant II mein hota hai.
explanation.en: With x<0, y>0, the point lies in Quadrant II.

question.hi: Origin se kisi point (x,y) ki distance √(x²+y²) hoti hai.
question.en: The distance of a point (x,y) from the origin is √(x²+y²).

explanation.hi: Sahi — ye distance formula ka special case hai jahan doosra point (0,0) hai.
explanation.en: True — this is a special case of the distance formula where the other point is (0,0).

notes.hi: Distance formula: AB = √[(x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²] — Pythagoras Theorem se derive hota hai
notes.en: Distance formula: AB = √[(x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²] — derived from the Pythagoras Theorem

notes.hi: Distance hamesha positive hoti hai — squares ki wajah se signs matter nahi karte
notes.en: Distance is always positive — squaring means signs don't matter

summary.hi: Ab tum coordinate plane samajh sakte ho aur do points ke beech distance nikaal sakte ho — chahe origin se ho ya kisi bhi do points ke beech. Agle lesson mein hum seekhenge ki ek line segment ko kisi given ratio mein kaise divide karte hain — Section Formula ke through.
summary.en: You can now understand the coordinate plane and find the distance between two points — whether from the origin or between any two points. Next, we'll learn how to divide a line segment in a given ratio — using the Section Formula.
